actions.action: Scratch a twig to check for green, moist tissue underneath
Look along the stems for leaf buds or new leaves
Bend a small twig to test whether it is flexible or brittle
In late spring, prune off twigs that are clearly dead
Replace the gravel around the base with 2–3 inches of pine bark, pine needles or shredded leaves
Apply an acidic azalea fertilizer such as Holly-tone after the plant leafs out
Improve the soil if it is clay or drains poorly
